provenance_note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in code-review-sage and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is the App Kit level-1 commit with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/code_review_sage and its BUILTIN_NAMES row); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that. GitHub was the capture's stand-in gh (capture/gh_stub), never the real one.
data_notes: The GitHub in these pictures is invented: the fernleaf-garden organisation, its seed-swap and planting-calendar repositories, their pull requests, diffs and people, and the signed-in user sam-fernleaf are served by capture/gh_stub/gh from capture/gh_stub/data.json. None of them exists on GitHub, so the links lead nowhere.
The repositories were added and the review setting changed through the app's own API (capture/scenes.json setup); the review itself was started from the page in the recorded walkthrough.
Every finding, its wording and its count came from a live model reading those diffs during the capture, so they differ from run to run.
Reviews at once was set to 1 for the capture, so the two reviews ran one after the other.
The live stills (hero, use-case-report, use-case-finding) were taken on the walkthrough's own gateway after it was recorded, so they show the same review as the recording.
